app.name: Company Central Platform
app.description: Identity, organization, access and workflow for every business system in the company.

auth.mfaDescription: Enter the six-digit code from your authenticator app.
auth.forgotDescription: Enter your username. If an account exists, we will send instructions.
auth.forgotSubmitted: If an account exists, instructions have been sent.
auth.lockedDescription: Too many failed attempts. Try again later or contact an administrator.
auth.changeDescription: This account requires a new password before you continue.
auth.signInLead: Use the account issued to you by your administrator.

errors.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.
errors.forbidden: You do not have permission to do this.
errors.tooManyRequests: Too many attempts. Wait a moment and try again.
errors.invalidCredentials: The username or password is incorrect. Repeated failures delay further attempts.
errors.mfaEnrolmentRequired: This action needs two-factor authentication, and your account has none enrolled. Set it up under Security, then try again.

users.title: Users
users.searchPlaceholder: Search by name, username or email
users.unlockDescription: The account was locked by repeated failed sign-ins. Unlocking lets them try again immediately.
users.disableDescription: They will not be able to sign in until the account is enabled again.
users.enableDescription: They will be able to sign in again.
users.createDescription: The account is created with a one-time password the person must change at first sign-in.
users.initialPasswordHint: A one-time handover credential. Choose something the person can type.

audit.title: Audit
audit.description: Who did what, to what, when, and from where.
audit.dateRangeRequired: Choose a date range to search.
audit.dateRangeTooWide: The range is too wide. Narrow it to 90 days or fewer.

employees.title: Employees
employees.description: People, their unit and their position.
employees.createDescription: An employee is an organizational record: their number, their name, and the unit they belong to. Salary, leave and contract are not here. Those belong to the HR application.
employees.employeeNumberHint: A stable, unique number that other systems use to refer to this employee.
employees.noUnitsTitle: No employee can be created yet
employees.noUnitsDescription: Every employee belongs to an organizational unit, and there are none. Build the structure first.
employees.transferDescription: Unit, position and manager together in one step, because a transfer is a single organizational fact.
employees.linkDescription: Connects this employee record to an account that signs in. They are separate things: an employee may have no account, and an account may belong to nobody on the payroll.
employees.attributesHint: An application's own notes about this person. The Platform stores them and never interprets them, which is why a key names the application that owns it.
employees.attributeKeyHint: Written as application.name, for example payroll.cost-centre. The namespace is what stops two systems colliding on the same word.
employees.attributeValueHint: Metadata about a person, not a place to keep a document or a credential.
employees.noAttributesDescription: No application has recorded anything about this person.
employees.attributeLooksLikeASecret: That looks like a credential, and it was not stored. An employee record is exported, backed up and broadly readable; secrets live in the secret store and are named by reference.
employees.attributeKeyInvalid: A key is written as application.name, using letters, digits, hyphens and underscores.
employees.attributeValueRequired: An attribute needs a value. Remove it instead of emptying it.
employees.attributeLimitReached: This person already carries fifty attributes. Remove one before adding another.

roles.title: Roles
roles.description: What a role grants, and where.
roles.name: Name
roles.assignDescription: The role decides what this user can do. The scope decides who to.
roles.revokeDescription: The user loses every permission this role carries, immediately.
roles.scopeUnitAndBelow: A unit and everything beneath it
roles.noAssignmentsDescription: This user holds no role, and so can reach no administrative screen.
roles.cannotEscalate: You cannot grant a permission you do not hold yourself.
roles.createDescription: A role is created empty. Its permissions are set afterwards, because naming a bundle and filling it with access are different decisions.
roles.codeHint: A stable code that cannot change once created, such as hr-manager.
roles.permissionsDescription: Choose what people holding this role can do. You cannot add a permission you do not hold yourself.
roles.systemRoleReadOnly: This role belongs to the Platform, which maintains it from the endpoints themselves. Its permissions cannot be edited.
roles.deactivateDescription: An inactive role grants nothing. Everyone holding it loses those permissions immediately, without erasing the record that they held them.
roles.noRolesDescription: The Platform has only the administrator role. Create narrower ones so that granting any access is not granting all of it.
roles.changedElsewhere: Somebody else changed this role while you had it open. Reload it and apply your change to what it says now.

organization.title: Organizational structure
organization.description: The company's units, each beneath the one it reports to.
organization.createDescription: The new unit is created beneath the selected unit, or at the top if none is selected.
organization.codeHint: A stable code that does not change, such as FIN or HR-01.
organization.moveDescription: The unit and everything beneath it move together. A unit cannot be moved inside itself.
organization.deactivateDescription: The unit will no longer appear in lists. A unit with active children or active employees cannot be deactivated.
organization.emptyDescription: Start with the company's top unit, then add what sits beneath it. An employee cannot be created before there is a unit for them.
organization.companyMissingTitle: The company is not defined yet
organization.companyMissingDescription: Everything here belongs to the company: units belong to it, and employees belong to units. Define the company first.
organization.companyCodeHint: A short, stable code that cannot change once set.
organization.positionsDescription: The company's job titles. A position describes what someone does in the organization, not what they may do in the software. That is what roles are for.
organization.levelHint: An optional number for ordering positions in the structure. Not a permission level.
organization.noPositionsDescription: Create job titles to attach to employees, and to route work by later.

security.title: Security
security.description: Two-factor authentication, and the actions that require your identity confirmed.
security.mfaWhy: Some actions, granting roles above all, ask you to confirm your identity again before they run. That confirmation is not possible without two-factor authentication.
security.enrolStep1: Open your authenticator app and add a new account using this key:
security.enrolStep2: Then enter the six-digit code the app shows:
security.disableDescription: Enter a current code from your app. Without it, anyone holding a stolen session could remove the protection that would have stopped them.
security.recoveryDescription: Save these somewhere safe now. They will not be shown again: they are stored hashed, and this is the only moment they are readable. Each one works once.
security.stepUpDescription: This action needs your identity confirmed recently. Enter the code from your authenticator app.
security.stepUpNotEnrolled: This action needs two-factor authentication, which is off for your account. Turn it on from the Security page, then try again.
security.sessionsDescription: Where this account is signed in right now. If you do not recognise a device, change your password. That ends every session except the one you are using.
security.noSessionsDescription: This is the only session open on your account.
security.historyDescription: Recent attempts on your account, successful and failed. An attempt you did not make is the earliest signal you will get that someone is trying your account.
security.noHistoryDescription: No sign-in attempts have been recorded on this account yet.
security.eventsDescription: What the Platform recorded about security: failed attempts, lockouts, second factors enrolled, elevations confirmed.
security.noEventsDescription: No security events were recorded in this range.

dashboard.unavailableHint: You do not hold the permission to read this figure.
dashboard.description: Where the Platform stands, and what is waiting on you.
dashboard.readAt: Read at {time}. Nothing on this page refreshes itself.

attention.heading: Needs your attention
attention.deadLettered: {count, plural, one {One event was given up on and will not be retried.} other {# events were given up on and will not be retried.}}
attention.outboxBehind: Event delivery is behind: {count, plural, one {one event is waiting} other {# events are waiting}}, {minutes, plural, one {the oldest for a minute} other {the oldest for # minutes}}.
attention.failingJobs: {count, plural, one {One background job failed on its last run.} other {# background jobs failed on their last run.}}
attention.suspendedSubscriptions: {count, plural, one {One subscription is suspended after repeated delivery failures.} other {# subscriptions are suspended after repeated delivery failures.}}
attention.securityEvents: {count, plural, one {One high-severity security event in the last twenty-four hours.} other {# high-severity security events in the last twenty-four hours.}}
attention.mfaOff: Two-step verification is off for your account. You cannot grant roles without it.
attention.unreadNotifications: {count, plural, one {One notification you have not read.} other {# notifications you have not read.}}
attention.noUnits: There is no organizational structure yet. No employee can exist before a unit does.
attention.noEmployees: The units exist but no employee does. Add employees to their units.
attention.oneUser: Yours is the only account. Create user accounts and grant them roles.

dashboard.noTasks: No task is waiting on your decision.

workflow.title: My tasks
workflow.instancesDescription: The approvals running on the Platform, and who decided what.
workflow.definitionsDescription: The registered approval processes. Applications register them; the Platform runs them and does not know what is being approved.
workflow.noTasksDescription: Nothing is waiting for your decision right now.
workflow.actDescription: Recorded with your name and the time, and it cannot be edited afterwards.
workflow.commentHint: Appears in the request's history for everybody who can see it.
workflow.noInstancesDescription: No approval has started yet. The systems that build on the Platform are what start them.
workflow.noDefinitionsDescription: Applications register their approval processes through the API. The Platform holds no business rule: thresholds, amounts and conditions stay in the system that owns the request.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: Messages the Platform has sent you.
notifications.noNotificationsDescription: You have not received any messages yet.
notifications.subject: Subject
notifications.preferencesDescription: Turn off what you do not need. Security notifications cannot be turned off: they tell you your account may be at risk, and the person most likely to want them silenced is whoever took it.
notifications.logDescription: What was sent and how it went. Messages that failed permanently stay here rather than disappearing.
notifications.noLogDescription: No message has been sent yet.

documents.title: Documents
documents.description: Files kept by the company, with who may see each one.
documents.searchHint: Matches the title of a document.
documents.titleHint: Left empty, the file name is used.
documents.categoryHint: A label of your own, such as contract or policy. Optional.
documents.tooLarge: That file is larger than this Platform accepts.
documents.typeNotAllowed: Files of that kind are not accepted.
documents.scanRejected: That file was refused by the malware scan.
documents.noDocumentsDescription: Nothing has been stored here, or nothing has been shared with you.
documents.deleteDescription: {title} will stop appearing in listings. Its content is kept for thirty days and can be restored during that time; after that it is destroyed permanently.
documents.accessLogHint: Every time this document was opened, and every time somebody tried and could not.
documents.accessLevelIs: You have {level} access to this document.
documents.subject: Who
documents.subjectIdHint: The identifier of the person, role or unit to share this with.
documents.subjectRequired: Say who this should be shared with.

applications.title: Applications
applications.description: The systems allowed to call this Platform, and the keys they call with.
applications.registerDescription: A registered application gets a permission namespace of its own and can be given roles. Registering one is the machine equivalent of creating an administrator.
applications.codeHint: The permission namespace, such as finance. Permanent once set.
applications.name: Name
applications.noApplicationsDescription: Nothing has been registered to call this Platform yet.
applications.label: Label
applications.labelHint: What this key is for, such as production or the nightly job.
applications.labelRequired: Give the key a label, so revoking the right one is possible later.
applications.tooManyCredentials: This application already holds two live keys. Revoke the one being replaced first.
applications.rotationHint: An application may hold two live keys at once. Issue the new one, deploy it, then revoke the old one when nothing has used it for long enough to be sure.
applications.secretShownOnceDetail: It is stored only as a hash and cannot be retrieved or resent. Copy it into your secret store now; losing it means issuing another key and revoking this one.
applications.rolesHint: An application holds the same roles as a person, at the same scopes, and may do only what they allow.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.description: The external services the Platform is allowed to call, and how they are behaving.
integrations.noProvidersDescription: Nothing has been registered for the Platform to call.
integrations.noCallsDescription: The Platform has not called this provider yet.
integrations.healthWindow: Health is from the last hour of calls, as at {checked}.
integrations.registerHint: The Platform may call this address and no other. Resilience settings arrive with the Platform defaults and are tuned afterwards.
integrations.registered: {name} is registered. It is switched off until you enable it.
integrations.codeHint: Short and stable. Callers name the provider by this, so it is not something to change later.
integrations.name: Name
integrations.baseAddressHint: Every call is built from this address and a relative path. The host must also be on the outbound allow-list, which is configuration rather than a field here.
integrations.codeTaken: A provider with this code already exists.
integrations.addressInvalid: That is not an address the Platform can call. Use an absolute http or https URL.
integrations.timeoutHint: Bounds one attempt, not the whole sequence.
integrations.retriesHint: Each attempt gets a fresh timeout. Zero means one try.
integrations.failuresHint: How many failures open the circuit, so a provider that is down stops costing a thread per call.
integrations.breakForHint: How long the circuit stays open before one call is allowed through to test the water.
integrations.concurrencyHint: A slow provider absorbs every thread the Platform has if nothing stops it. The symptom is not a slow integration; it is a Platform that stops answering.
integrations.redactedFieldsHint: Comma separated. Blanked before the call log row is written, not when it is read: hiding a value at read time leaves it in the database, the next export and the next backup.
integrations.credentialReferenceHint: The name of a secret, such as integrations/acme/api-key. The value lives in the secret store and there is no field in the Platform that could hold one.
integrations.credentialValueRefused: That looks like a secret rather than the name of one, and it was not stored. This field holds a reference such as integrations/acme/api-key; the value belongs in the secret store.
integrations.resilienceOutOfRange: One of those numbers is outside what the Platform accepts.
integrations.subscriptionsHint: The other direction: the Platform posts to a business system when something happens, so it does not have to poll. Every delivery is signed, and goes out through the same allow-list as every other outbound call.
integrations.noSubscriptionsDescription: No business system has asked to be told when something happens.
integrations.subscriptionHint: The Platform will post to this address when one of the named events happens, signed with the secret you name.
integrations.subscriptionEndpointHint: Where to post. The host must be on the outbound allow-list; it is checked now rather than when an event fires.
integrations.subscriptionEventsHint: Choose each event by name. There is deliberately no way to ask for everything: you would receive events added years later and find out by failing to parse them.
integrations.subscriptionSecretHint: The name of a secret, such as integrations/acme/webhook-secret. The value lives in the secret store, and nothing is ever sent unsigned.
integrations.subscriptionResumed: The subscription was resumed, and the failures that suspended it were cleared.
integrations.subscriptionEndpointRefused: The Platform is not allowed to call that address. Add the host to the outbound allow-list first.
integrations.subscriptionEndpointInvalid: That is not an address the Platform will post to. Use an absolute http or https URL with no credentials in it.
integrations.subscriptionEventsRequired: Name at least one event type.
integrations.subscriptionSecretRequired: Name the secret to sign with. Nothing is ever sent unsigned.
integrations.noDeliveriesDescription: No event matching this subscription has happened yet.
integrations.subscriptionEventTypesUnknown: The Platform does not send one or more of these event types, so nothing would ever be delivered. Choose from the list.
integrations.subscriptionNoEventTypes: The list of event types could not be loaded.

configuration.title: Configuration
configuration.description: How the Platform behaves, and which capabilities are switched on.
configuration.valueHint: Leave empty to clear the override and fall back to the default.
configuration.reasonHint: Why, in your words. Six months later the value explains what, and only this explains why.
configuration.scopeHint: The narrowest value that matches wins. Leaving the value empty removes the override at this scope and falls back to the next one out.
configuration.secretRefused: That looks like a secret. Settings are stored in plaintext and appear in backups and exports, so a secret belongs in the secret store and is named here by reference.
configuration.neverChangedDescription: This setting is still at whatever it was declared with.
configuration.flagsHint: A flag can be turned off without a deployment. Off is off however it is targeted.
configuration.targetNoUnits: No organizational units have been created.
configuration.targetNoneHint: Nothing selected: this flag reaches everybody when it is on.
configuration.targetSomeHint: Only the roles and units selected below.
configuration.targetUnitHint: A unit reaches everybody in it and in every unit below it.

operations.title: Operations
operations.description: What the Platform's own machinery has been doing.
operations.noJobsDescription: Nothing has been recorded. A job appears here the first time it runs.
operations.noRunsDescription: Nothing has been recorded for this job.
operations.readAt: Read at {time}. Nothing on this page refreshes itself.
operations.outboxHint: Events are written with the change that caused them and delivered afterwards. A backlog means delivery is behind, not that anything was lost.
operations.deadLetteredHint: These stopped being retried and need somebody to look at them.
